speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When the Act was introduced in 2005, there were just 170,000 strata units.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Strata developments are premised on a unique concept of community-based property ownership.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Subsidiary proprietors (SPs) individually own their lots, but everything outside of those lots is shared.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This entails collective ownership of common property and joint responsibility for the upkeep of shared areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In short, SPs need to cooperate and collaborate as they self-govern and maintain their own estates.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: BMSMA provides the legal framework for them to do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: From time to time, there have been calls to introduce more prescriptive legislation, particularly to resolve disputes between SPs, to spell everything out in crystal clear detail, with no room for discretion.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But this is probably not the best way to proceed, as each development has unique characteristics, including demographic of SPs, size, age, interests and location.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It also has its own set of circumstances and concerns.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It will be very difficult to have one-size-fits-all legislation that can satisfy all stakeholders in all developments.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the Act has been designed to empower MCSTs to manage their own affairs and make decisions relevant to their needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Ultimately, it is about striking a balance between maintaining the flexibility that underpins self-governance, while having sufficient oversight and structure to prevent abuse of the system.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And this is the thinking that underpins our proposed amendments to the Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We started a comprehensive review of BMSMA in 2012.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also took into account views given through forum letters, emails and other channels.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have considered them and incorporated many into the amendments that are before this House today.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, one amendment will now require SPs to give explicit consent before they can be nominated and elected into an MCST council.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While this may seem so obvious as to not necessitate express legislation, we had received feedback that some SPs had been elected into office without their knowledge.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the feedback that we received was very useful in helping us to craft this Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Broadly speaking, the amendments focus on three areas: first, setting clear boundaries for good governance and transparency; second, safeguarding SP interests; and third, clarifying existing provisions to facilitate stakeholders' understanding of their roles and responsibilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, we want to set clear boundaries, roles and responsibilities to enhance governance and transparency.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To begin with, we want to better define the duties and responsibilities of developers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Developers are responsible for the design and construction of projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They are also key stakeholders during the handing over of projects and after the constitution of MCSTs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, under clause 18, we propose to require that developers not only convene the first annual general meeting (AGM), but chair it, too.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is in light of feedback that some developers have devolved the duty of presiding over the first AGM to managing agents (MAs).

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a result, SPs often felt that their concerns, such as workmanship defects in their units or common property, were not expeditiously brought to the attention of the developer.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also want to ensure that the handover from the developer to the MCST is in order.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is to ensure that MCSTs should not have to take over deficits that they were not responsible for.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the light of the increasing adoption of prefabricated bathroom units (PBUs), we will also require developers to hand over the manufacturer's manuals to the MCST.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is in addition to other important documents like as-built drawings and warranties.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will help SPs maintain the installations in their lots in future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: After the handover, MCSTs become responsible for governance and management.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A large part of this responsibility is vested in the management council.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have received examples where a single council member concurrently holds all three offices of Chairperson, Secretary and Treasurer.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, we recognise that smaller MCSTs face practical difficulties in getting sufficient people to fill each of these three offices.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Hence, we will, under the existing section 134 of the Act, exempt MCSTs with 10 or fewer lots from this requirement, provided they pass a resolution by consensus to permit the council member in question to hold more than one concurrent key office.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This exemption will cover less than 5% of existing MCSTs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The remaining MCSTs are larger developments that should be able to find additional council members to take up key posts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we are adding more safeguards to protect the interests of SPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was a strata development which was seriously at risk of falling into extensive disrepair because of disputes between the council and some SPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Chairperson, after being ousted, refused to relinquish his position and authorise the newly elected council members as bank signatories.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The bank subsequently froze the MCST's accounts so the MCST could not pay its service providers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: During this time, the development could not continue with its regular maintenance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, the objective is to ensure that management and routine maintenance are not impeded while internal issues are sorted out.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The principle of strata living remains one of self-governance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the bar is set high before this provision can be invoked.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: A prescribed number of SPs has to make a written request to the Commissioner.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The latter must also be of the opinion that official management is necessary, for example, the mismanagement is so severe as to likely jeopardise the health or safety of SPs and occupiers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Separately, Members would have read in media reports about ‘‘proxy wars" at general meetings where some proxy holders garnered enough undirected proxy votes to dominate proceedings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was a case a few years ago where three council members held more than 60% of the votes at a general meeting.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This allowed them to effectively block attempts to remove them.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Any proxy instruments held in excess will be treated as having no effect.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was overwhelming support for this proposal during public consultations.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many respondents felt that this would help rein in abuse and the ensuing spats.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As an added safeguard, we will be prescribing an improved form of instrument to appoint a proxy.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will allow the proxy giver to explicitly direct his proxy to vote as he intended.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is an improvement from the current situation where proxy holders are essentially given "blank cheques".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We recognise that these proposals cannot totally eradicate the problem of proxy abuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Several SPs can theoretically still come together to coordinate and exercise their proxy votes collectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But again, it is about striking a balance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Abolishing the proxy system would mean that any SP unable to attend general meetings would be completely unrepresented.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, in our view, the 2% cap is a calibrated point between tightening the system and keeping it practicable.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On the issue of fair representation, clause 38 or the new section 53A provides that each class of use in a mixed-use development will be given a reserved seat in the council.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Different classes of uses have different needs, so it is important for each to have a "voice".

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The classes of use include residential, commercial and single independent lot groups like hotels and serviced residences.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There was feedback about a residential and retail development where the council was dominated by retail SPs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This resulted in a skewed decision by the council to lease common property cheaply to the retail shops in the development.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The facility of reserved seats for each user class will go some way to address over-domination by any one user class and put each group in a more equitable position in managing the MCST.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Another amendment, at clause 15, reframes the requirement in section 18 for developers to seek approval from the Commissioner of Buildings for the maximum rate for maintenance charges it collects.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Currently, developers need to seek the Commissioner's approval for maintenance charges, but we do not mandate when approval must be obtained.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Often, developers seek approval just before handing over the strata lots to purchasers.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have received feedback that some purchasers were, at the point of sale, misled into thinking that the maintenance charges would be low, only to be shocked years later that the actual charges were almost more than double.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The proposed change will support amendments to the statutory forms for Option to Purchase and Sale and Purchase Agreement, which require the approved maintenance charge rate to be reflected.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will ensure that the maximum quantum for charges will be transparent at the point of sale.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Next, we want to strengthen an existing provision to facilitate SPs' installation of safety equipment in their own lots.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: While an existing prescribed by-law states that SPs cannot be prevented from installing any structure or device that prevents harm to children, SPs are also required to seek the MCST's approval for installations which affect the appearance of the building.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There have been cases of MCSTs vetoing SPs' installation of safety grilles on the basis that the designs affected the building's appearance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But a new section 37A(2) will place the onus on SPs to ensure that their installations maintain a certain uniformity of appearance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In this regard, developers and MCSTs are encouraged to provide design guidelines for such installations upfront, to guide SPs in achieving the overall desired appearance.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, we will amend some existing provisions for clarity.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is because such services and elements serve more than one strata lot, notwithstanding their physical location within one lot.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But I should clarify that defining floor slabs as part of common property will not change the existing presumption clause for strata developments that the upper floor unit is responsible for inter-floor water leakage, unless it is able to prove otherwise.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Related to the management of common property, we will make clear what changes to common property require a special resolution.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This amendment was triggered by a recent dispute over an MCST's intent to permanently remove a facility on common property.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: An SP challenged the MCST's mandate, as the Act currently only stipulates installation and provision of additional facilities as improvement works.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition, we propose to make explicit the decisions that require ordinary resolutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, the Act is currently silent on whether determining the amount of maintenance contributions and imposing restrictions on the council can be decided via ordinary resolutions.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It was previously considered unnecessary to specify since an ordinary resolution is the default mode for an MCST's decision-making.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, we recognise that providing more explicit provisions will facilitate laypersons' self-governing efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Bill, therefore, makes several amendments to the Act to specify where ordinary resolutions are required for various decisions an MCST can make.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond enhancing the Act, we will help stakeholders to better understand their roles and responsibilities in relation to the self-governing framework.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As many SPs find the BMSMA complex and technical, BCA will publish a series of Strata Management Guides covering areas where the bulk of feedback has been received.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These guides will clarify the various provisions and provide references for good practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: More importantly, these guides will be presented in clear and simple terms to facilitate understanding.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There will also be targeted efforts to level up the competencies of council members of MCSTs and MAs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, BCA will continue to hold regular seminars for council members, especially first timers, to guide them on their statutory duties and responsibilities under BMSMA.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, we will raise the bar for MAs and help MCSTs select better performing ones.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To do this, we are working with the relevant industry associations to develop an accreditation framework for MA firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The accreditation framework will also feature a robust competency training component to ensure that MAs can deliver quality service.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will share more details on these plans when ready.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This self-governing approach helps to provide a broad and flexible framework that caters to the unique circumstances and interests of each MCST in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The strata system works well when there are cooperation and commitment from stakeholders.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We hope that the proposed amendments will help SPs as they step up and get involved in their respective councils and estates.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They are also subject to annual Town Council Management Reports to ensure that they are kept on their toes in servicing the residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In contrast, strata-titled properties get a lot more flexibility in terms of regulations and management.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The downside is, this can result in slack and allows inefficiency to set in.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Clearly, the amendments to the Bill are in direct response to a series of feedback concerning management woes in strata-titled properties.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: While strata-titled properties are private properties, the Government has a duty to ensure that the welfare of the people living in these properties are not being compromised.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill is of great relevance to me as there are several condominiums in my Group Representation Constituency (GRC).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have discussed it with residents, management committee (MC) members and others, and I am pleased to use this opportunity to share their feedback.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The majority of these amendments are welcome as it is believed that they will do right by the residents and safeguard their rights to the quality of life that they pay for.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Concerned that window grilles would affect the seamless aesthetics of a condominium, the installation of such grilles is sometimes disallowed by the MCSTs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This can be a dilemma for those who have young children or elderly members at home.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Aside from safety grilles, I hope that the amendment will also be extended to other items, especially in the interest of safety for everyone, such as replacement of windows.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In some of the condominiums in my constituency, I received feedback about one or two persons holding many proxy lots.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many residents have been telling me that in one particular condominium, there is a property agent who owns a unit but she does not live in that condominium.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But every time when an AGM is approaching, she will go round collecting proxies even standing at the guard house to collect proxies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This enabled her to sway outcomes at the AGM according to her desires even if the decision was, in fact, not a popular one or beneficial to the majority.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The amendment will not only lead to a fairer decision-making process but will hopefully encourage residents and owners to be more actively involved in running their own estate.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As the role of a Treasurer is heavily involved with the management of the finances, it would also be prudent to set some criteria to eliminate unsuitable candidates.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, the appointee should not have a criminal record, especially if it relates to financial crimes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Realistically speaking, it would be impractical to enforce mandatory background checks on all would-be treasurers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But it is important to have a treasurer with good integrity and with some knowledge of accounts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This should help to create another viable avenue for getting funds for maintenance, thus reducing problems of poor or inadequate maintenance due to lack of funds and the need to raise service fees every year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, when the rental fees for substantial amounts of common properties to commercial enterprises, such as a food and beverage (F&B) outlet, are involved, it should be a requirement to seek approval from the SPs through a special resolution to channel the money into the fund.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And all the transactions on renting out the common property area should be arm's-length dealings.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: On approval of maintenance charges before sale launch of the property, this is a welcome move, but it would be even better if the published charges could also include the expenses per share value for three years, taking into account a 3% per annum inflation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Additionally, the estimated time and expenses for the first replacement of lifts, pumps and water tanks should also be made known.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will not only help MCSTs to better manage finances but also give buyers a heads up.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Some young buyers, especially, put their deposits on a dream condominium they can barely afford, without taking the monthly maintenance fees into consideration.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If an MA has been appointed for a three-year term, it might seem to be a waste of time and resources to do an annual review on his or her performance during the AGM.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, I believe the reason this was stipulated in the first place is because three years is a long period of time and could breed complacency if there are no reviews in place.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: A long-time trusted MA would not require such frequent reviews, but there should be an option in every strata-titled property to appoint MAs for shorter terms, such as a one-year term.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Once the MCST has been formally constituted, it is important that the balance of monies transferred by the developer from the maintenance fund to the MCST's bank account be a positive amount.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will ensure a smooth handover without deficit in the account and it would discourage misuse of funds.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Often times, developers and MAs hold on to the documents, regardless of whether it is done intentionally or not.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I would also like to suggest to go one step further in listing down what are the documents to be handled over from the developer to the MCST.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Recently, I have just meditated between the residents and the developers.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Transparency pertaining to management matters is important, but so is privacy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The switch to managing data by electronic means will no doubt make matters much more convenient for those involved.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Given the rise in cybercrimes, security measures must be in place to prevent data theft.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And as it has now become a requirement to display not just the names but also addresses of eligible voters for an AGM, it would be prudent to ensure that the data is not given unnecessary exposure.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The duration of display should be stipulated, after which it should be removed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: About four hours after the AGM would be a reasonable amount of time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Online payment modes should also be allowed and encouraged, as they are more convenient for property owners, and it is also easier to keep records of transactions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   This amendment will provide more protection for residents living in condominiums, especially with clauses, such as one person cannot hold multiple votes, and that the MCSTs cannot disallow residents to install window grills.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I suggest that upon launching the property, the MCSTs publish the maintenance charges for the first three years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will give the buyers a heads-up, especially those young buyers who have less savings.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In addition, the Treasurer should not be the same person as the Chairman, and must disclose whether he has any criminal record, in order to better protect the residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I support the Bill and I believe it will help to facilitate more fairness and professionalism in the management of strata-titled properties.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Amongst other things, this Bill aims to improve the governance and transparency in the running of strata-titled developments.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are three points which I would like to touch on today.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have to recognise that many residents are rather apathetic and being appointed as part of the management council is, indeed, a "thankless" job.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Right now, the quorum for a general meeting is set at 30% of share values of all lots and, if the quorum is not met within half an hour, the meeting may be held if two or more SPs are present in person.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While I understand the necessity for a meeting to carry on, I feel the minimum of just two under the "half hour" rule is a bar set too low.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If two or more SPs challenge the decisions within 30 days of being informed of the decisions made, then a new general meeting has to be called.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second point I would like to talk about is the checks and balances in place for the appointment of service providers, such as the MA or companies that carry out repair and maintenance works for the development.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If the MCST members appoint their own companies to carry out service for the condominium, are the prices to be paid for such services reflective of general market rate and will the MCST pursue claims against such service providers if the standard of services delivered is poor?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the current regulations or guidelines governing situations where members of the MCST have interests in such service providers?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It would be good if there is a requirement for a minimum of three quotes or where they are barred from providing the service.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The third and final point that I would like to bring up is the responsibility of the property developer regarding the appointment of an interim MA.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the early stages after a condominium project's completion, the property developer appoints an interim MA until the first AGM is held.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The impression is that the interim MA is beholden to the developer for its appointment and would wish to be appointed for other condominium projects and, as such, would not be motivated to pursue the developer to rectify defects during the Defects Liability Period (DLP).

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Usually, the DLP is only for 12 months after the unit is handed over and, usually, by the time an AGM is held and a new MA is appointed, DLP is already over.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This would provide enough time for the new MA to rectify any defect which is not resolved by the interim MA.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope STB will consider the issues I have raised today.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Notwithstanding my comments and suggestions, I reiterate my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While I do agree with most of the amendments here, I have some concerns and require some clarifications regarding this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will first talk about the suspension of Management Council and appointment of official management.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are very stern if not drastic measures, potentially threatening the status quo of the management of an MCST.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will this recourse be abused by minority owners in the MCST who may, for reasons unrelated to the conditions in sections 126A and 126B, be disagreeable with the current management of an estate, for example, rival owners who may have lost out in MC elections or are disagreeable with the current management's plans or management priorities?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am concerned that the condition stated in clause 126B(1b) is too general and may be open to unintended abuses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Perhaps, the requirements should have been spelt out in greater detail in this Bill, or even in the subsidiary legislation behind the Act, for greater certainty and to prevent abuse.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I next go on to the expansion in the definition of "common property".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is an expanded definition of common property under the interpretation section in the new section 2(c) with four areas, namely, (i) pipes, wires, cables or ducts used or capable of being used by two or more occupiers; (ii) the cubic space enclosed by a structure enclosing pipes, wires, cables or ducts; (iii) any structural element of the building; and (iv) the waterproof membrane attached to an external wall or roof.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: While the inclusion of the above areas may provide helpful access and management by the MCST and MA, I am concerned whether it will also provide more grounds for misunderstanding or disputes between owners and MCST or MA.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There are likely to be cases that may be different from the five examples given and may not fit in clearly to the straitjacket of the four areas in section 2(c).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the other hand, the new four areas in section 2(c) may create new scenarios where disagreement or dispute may result.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us take example (d) in the new section.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It appears that a fire sprinkler protection system is now part of common property.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Owners of an office strata unit may now need MCST's consent to make changes to the fire sprinkler system within their strata unit.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And if so, what if an MA or MCST unreasonably withhold consent to the work intended or requires something to be done to the disagreement of the owners for reasons of costs, design or otherwise?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What are the options open to owners in such a situation if they do not agree with the MA or MCST?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some owners may take the opportunity to push the boundary and push certain responsibility to their MCST.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I next touch on the area of imposing budget.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The above two items of expenses are new additions under this Bill and inserted in sections 38(3)(d) and (e).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Organising of social, cultural, educational or sports activities is arguably not new to condominiums or private estates as such.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Neither is the need for MC to use legal services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, what is new is the budgetary requirement in section 38(3A), that is to say, the need to have the budget be approved for these items at an AGM.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, the need to go to an EOGM for these two items of expenditure may be cumbersome for not just the MC but the residents as well.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The attendance of residents in most MCST AGM is hardly ever glowing.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the MC wants to hold a simple event for the residents which was never budgeted previously, it would be put off by the trouble to try and hold the EOGM, not to mention the likely difficulty of getting a quorum.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Residents may feel that it may not justify their time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It may stifle attempts by active MCs to constantly come up with new activities to encourage residents to fraternise and also the building up of community relations within the estate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would this lead to external organisations, whether commercial or statutory, coming up with sponsorships of events for their own agenda, particularly given that budget is always an issue which affects MCSTs?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would it not be better to have a more general regulation leaving it to owners in each MCST to decide what kind of budgetary constraints or authorisation they wish to impose on their MC?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This can be done at AGMs or even through individual by-laws of each MCST.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Does the law need to interfere now with this new budgetary requirement?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I would touch on the area of improvements which increase the floor area.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may serve to protect innocent buyers who may not be informed of the alleged breach or any related action the MC may be taking against the existing owner.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: In fact, it has been some 12 years since the last update.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is an important Bill, with a significant proportion of our population today staying in private apartments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The level of sophistication of our property owners today requires the MCs to be more professional, with extremely high governance standards.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have several comments and queries as follows.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The guidelines are clearer now with better definition, and these are clearly outlined to avoid abuse and misinterpretations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: However, what about side-to-side leakages, which do happen as well?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can there be some guidelines or advisory on this as well, as I have had to handle a few cases in my constituency and they drag on for a long time?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Of course, case-to-case considerations, such as the bathroom or the toilet of one unit adjacent to the bedroom of another unit could perhaps commonsensically assume that it is coming from one particular unit.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But there may issues that may arise in individual cases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Thirdly, for mixed development MCSTs, there are always issues in trying to balance the needs and wishes of the different stakeholders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Even with the allocation of one seat for each property user group, there is still a loophole because the proportion of each type of stakeholders is different.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For example, 70%-80% could be residential and 20%-30% could be commercial entities within that development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I noticed that this has brought on a variety of issues as the demands and needs of the different groups vary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: That is also why the combination of residential and commercial entities in the same development prove to have some challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there more innovative ways to handle some of these challenges moving forward?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Fourth, knowing the demands on MCSTs and MC members, it will be very useful and helpful for those elected to have an understanding of the regulatory framework and their commitments under the provision of the Bill.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Is BCA considering making it compulsory for new members elected to attend a course explaining the regulatory framework, roles and responsibilities and other topics which include budgeting, maintenance requirements, use of funds, minute keeping and even conduct of general meetings?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This can certainly help the empowerment of council members and ensure they are stepping forward to be nominated as an informed choice.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have organised some sessions informally in my ward whereby BCA and the other agencies are invited to share and respond to queries and doubts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We have had very good feedback from the MCSTs and MAs as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I hope the Minister can address some of these issues and clarify the doubts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Bill will greatly improve the management of properties.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I want to put on record my appreciation for the contributions of members of the public and various stakeholders who had given their feedback and recommendations over the last few years.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We are now benefiting from their collective wisdom.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just have a few more suggestions for the Ministry's consideration.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there remains a possibility that some MAs will not be able to function properly during the first months of the estate's operations or during the transition period from the developer to the MA appointed by the MCST.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, in addition to the prohibition for a council member to hold the position of Treasurer concurrently as a Chairperson or a Secretary, all councillors should be required to make declarations to ensure there will be no conflict of interest in all appointments of contractors for the estate's maintenance.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In some cases, after an open tender, an estate may face a limited number of choices for contractors, some of whom may be related to council members.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As we see the completion of more development projects, we encounter more cases of dispute between new home owners and developers.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Residents in condominiums should be encouraged to form Neighbourhood Committees (NCs) whose objective is fulfilling the social needs of the residents, so that the MA can focus on and be primarily responsible for estate maintenance.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Both the MA and NC should work closely together for the benefit of the residents while enabling and encouraging individual responsibility.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There are several enhancements introduced in this Bill.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For example, by establishing special subcommittees to oversee or approve certain expenditure projects, the MCST could introduce such committees to enable a separate group to pass decisions or indirectly garner more proxy votes through other options.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Is the new proxy system applicable for all decision matters that need to be passed by MCSTs or only for major decisions during AGMs?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: If it is the latter, would it not be effective to consider compulsory enforcement of proxy voting, specific to certain categories of estate matters, that is, sinking funds, land strata-related matters?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For smaller developments, for example, the walk-up apartments and mixed development condominiums, I understand that some do not have sufficient members to form a council and thus appoints the Chairperson and two other key members on a rotation basis.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Such smaller developments may have fewer common facilities but due to the age of their development and class of use, there is likely a more pressing need for collective decisions to be made in upkeeping the place.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I have such condominiums in my constituency and, with age, some of the developments have more residents who are elderly and do not effectively have much sinking funds available.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Such disputes arise and there is a need to replace or repair the facilities for safety reasons but it is always opposed by a few members.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: How can the other SPs seek assistance for intervention to mediate a resolution?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Second, consent of nominees for election as council members.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I certainly support this change and feel this should have been the default arrangement when BMSMA was first introduced.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Council members are residents of the development and any service they provide to the estate is considered voluntary.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It is unfair to have anyone nominated and elected without their knowledge or not of their own free will.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The real challenge for many developments is, however, a lack of willing individuals who want to step forward and serve, given the responsibilities and thankless chores within the estate.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Third, mandated approval of maintenance charges before sale of units.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The approach is useful in preventing wide disparity between what is committed at sales launches and the actual charge upon Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP).

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Can BCA elaborate how the Commissioner assesses the proposed maintenance charges are justifiable for the facilities that have yet to be built?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Before issuance of TOP, if the site assessment reflects that the prior approved maintenance charge by the commissioner may be insufficient to cover subsequent maintenance, are the developers allowed to make adjustments, capped at a specified rate, or will BCA request for actions to be taken before TOP?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: To prevent such risk, should a range be suggested instead to ensure the approved maintenance charge have adequate considerations for facilities under frequent operation or for post-warranty periods?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I would suggest BCA further consider this area for MAs in future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: It would be helpful if BCA could consider the need for MA companies to comply with some basic service standards, staff qualifications and audits conducted on its procurement processes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A council member should not be the Chairperson for more than two terms but he may run for the offices of Treasurer or Secretary during his third term as council member.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Hopefully, such a regulatory requirement would encourage all owners to step forward and participate more actively in the management of their estate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A common complaint is that it is difficult to find volunteers to serve in the MC.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, it is only fair that all the owners of a development do their part and take turns to be council members.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They can also encourage their neighbours to join the council as part of a concerted effort to renew the talent pool.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such an arrangement will also minimise the problem of a few owners dominating the management agenda for the estate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As MC decisions are usually based on the needs of the majority, small groups with real needs, such as the handicapped and the elderly, may have a hard time gaining approval for certain installations in their estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some owners had to take their councils to Court, as we had seen for parents wishing to install safety grilles in their balconies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will allow MAs and MCSTs to communicate with all owners and residents expediently, more efficiently and cost effectively.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents should also be encouraged to submit their feedback, complaints and suggestions likewise.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is in line with our national objective to build a Smart Nation, to tap upon opportunities offered by digital technologies and keep Singapore a leading city.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The amendments provide greater clarity to the responsibilities held by MCSTs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I would like to seek some clarifications on the Bill.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I welcome the new provision to encourage MCSTs to put in place design guidelines for safety grilles to prevent children from falling from heights.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, home owners will be required to ensure that the grilles look aesthetically compatible with the building.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am sure Members will agree that aesthetics is inherently subjective and this could lead to potential conflicts if the design sense of the home owners and the MCST is not aligned.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This was precisely what happened in a case that made the news last year, when a condominium resident wanted to install window grilles to prevent his children from falling, but was blocked by the MC.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: While I can understand that the MCSTs would not want to ruin their building aesthetics with unsightly grilles, I feel that the safety of vulnerable children must take priority.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry, therefore, clarify if there can be a clear definition of "safety" for parties to refer to, so that similar disputes can be resolved quickly instead of undergoing a long legal dispute?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This discovery came about only after an industrial building caught fire in May this year, which claimed a precious life and prompted this review.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With a rapidly ageing population, there is a need to look after seniors living in old private apartments without lifts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are several such apartments in my constituency and, during my house visits, the elderly residents living in the upper floors often tell me that they cannot navigate the stairs and feel "imprisoned" within their own homes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can the Ministry help these groups of elderly residents?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If left on their own, it is unlikely that the lifts would ever get installed due to the differing interests between the residents staying on the higher floors and those on the lower floors.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to touch on the importance of neighbourliness and the limitations that the MCSTs face currently.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My constituency has a large majority of private estates.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Recently, I had to deal with a dispute similar to the infamous Astrid Hill rain tree case.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In gist, the leaves of the trees planted by one MCST had dropped on the grounds of another MCST.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This is a daily affair and arguments often occur over whose responsibility it was to deal with the problem.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To resolve such and other similar disagreements, would the Ministry consider setting up a mediation board within a cluster of MCSTs or by districts?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would help to provide a neutral platform for the MCSTs to resolve disputes amicably before resorting to litigation, which could be a costly process.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I believe that we need to take a step further to specify the composition of MCSTs, which will go a long way towards ensuring that decisions are made with the long-term interests of residents in mind.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Are there any selection criteria to be elected as a council member or to hold key positions, such as the chairperson, secretary or treasurer?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Should there be a requirement for such council members, especially those holding key positions, to be Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Having some form of minimum criteria to govern the composition of the MCSTs would help safeguard against those seeking to use management rights for personal gains and ensure that decisions made by the council would be most well-meaning for its residents in the long term.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It would also be good to spell out clearly how monies from the management fund may be disbursed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is there a limit on how much the MCST can be authorised to spend?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, some residents have expressed concerns to me that legal costs can be enormous when the MCST pursues or defends a legal case.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would there be a limit that requires a vote before the MCST can authorise such an expense?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It would be quite a stretch to call such AGMs held in such a manner as transparent when the residents are not well-represented.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Meetings should also be held only when the quorum is met so that decisions will be representative of the residents' interests.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am sure that these efforts to improve transparency and governance will be appreciated by the residents in the long term.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, I would like to clarify the following.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This should result in greater certainty of the costs to the tenants and residents.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It could also help ensure that developers act as greater stewards, ensuring better planning and are more careful of incurring any incidental expenditure.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Having said that, how is this maximum rate of maintenance charges computed and how often is this reviewed?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 37A is a welcomed amendment that helps to safeguard lives and works around past rigidities that building managers may hold.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Allowing home owners/SPs flexibility to install safety equipment that does not impact the building's structure is a reasonable change to the law.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: However, the owners/proprietors must be responsible enough to ensure that only contractors with safety track record are called upon to do such installation for home safety measures and not, when doing so, endangers the safety of others or the condition of the structures could potentially cause damage.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: As for section 126B(5), what would be a guideline relating to the remuneration of an OM and how often does the Commissioner review this?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: It is good that safeguards are in place.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 126B(4) includes the provision to rectify any foul play that could arise in terms of underpayment or overpayment.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is a positive change and I welcome it.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In the amendment to the First Schedule, clause 17(5) clearly outlines the number of proxy votes one can hold so as to prevent any abuse by a single resident in the estate.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is a rule that is upheld at most professional bodies and this is much welcomed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Better governance and transparency are welcomed in light of the numerous cases brought to the STB and media on disputes involving SPs and MCSTs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a departure from the current provisions of section 18 read with section 16, where, in practice, see developers obtaining approval from the Commissioner just before TOP issuance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This amendment will provide some comfort to buyers who can better assess their affordability since the property maintenance cost will be more accurately reflected at time of sale.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In practice, the amendment means developers will have to project the maintenance charges payable years before property projects are completed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify what happens if the maintenance charges have to be increased due to inflation or other costs?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the long run, this will not benefit SPs, if the maintenance charges are insufficient to cover the costs of the MCST running the property or if, on the other hand, it is, in fact, excessive.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, the Minister can consider incorporating flexible provisions which allow the rate of maintenance charges, approved by the Commissioner, to be adjusted within a certain range based on market rate at the time of TOP.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means the charges can either be increased or reduced.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This range can be provided to buyers in the Sale and Purchase Agreements as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify how this percentage threshold is derived?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Presumably, if the 30% quorum can be formed, motions can be passed to resolve disputes and issues without requiring the need to invoke sections 126A and 126B.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, can the Minister clarify how a slightly lower threshold of 20% of the aggregate share value of total lots accompanying a written request serves to provide SPs with an additional remedy in such dire circumstances?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the rationale is to provide an interim remedy for MCSTs in deadlock facing situations involving health or safety concerns, perhaps the threshold criteria ought to be tweaked such that the Commissioner is provided with discretion and full powers to appoint an OM as long as it is satisfied that there is a health and safety concern.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, as the other Members have raised, can the Minister also provide further clarifications on the definition of what "health and safety concerns" mean?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, I want to commend the Ministry of National Development (MND) for the extensive public consultation it has carried out with regard to these amendments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The public consultations and focus group panel dialogues since 2012 are very welcomed and this has engaged and empowered the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The revised proxy system is applicable for all decisions made at any general meeting, and not just AGMs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Chan also asked how to ensure that the tightened proxy system is not circumvented.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She raised the possibility of a council forming subcommittees to approve and oversee certain projects, thereby making decisions without the general body's involvement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is a natural check against this happening.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Joan Pereira suggested restricting the number of terms for the Chairperson, Secretary and Treasurer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is not the case for the Chairperson and Secretary whose duties are more administrative.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I agree that a regular renewal of council Members, especially the leadership positions, is ideal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the reality is that many MCSTs face challenges in getting sufficient SPs to step forward.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we need to find a balance between wanting to encourage participation and not creating a larger problem of MCSTs being unable to form a council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is because the Bill requires all council offices to be relinquished for re-election at every AGM.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the situation where there are small councils with two or three lots.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And this should cover less than 5% of existing MCSTs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Needless to say, in such situations, we will encourage these MCSTs to put in place the necessary governance measures catering to situations where some of these officeholders wear more than one hat, and possibly for prolonged durations of time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked if there are more innovative ways to balance the needs of different stakeholders in mixed-use developments.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She felt that the allocation of one seat for each user group on the council may be inadequate because it may not account for the proportion of share values held by each user group.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But Assoc Prof Fatimah is correct that it does not ensure that each user group is represented in the exact same proportion as their share value would hold.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This would be, unfortunately, quite a prescriptive method to ensure that everyone has a "voice" in the council.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And this is not to say that SPs of specific user groups cannot step forward in AGMs to make their views known clearly and directly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Developers are encouraged to design their mixed-use developments under a two-tier management corporation (MC) scheme.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This scheme has a main MC for the entire development at the first tier, and subsidiary MC of the individual user groups at the second tier.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The sub-MCs can then manage their own needs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, they can make their own by-laws and effect improvements to the limited common property which is for the exclusive use and enjoyment of that user group.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each sub-MC will also have a reserved seat in the main council to have a say where the common property is shared with the main MC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Yee Chia Hsing touched on the issue of conflict of interest, particularly in the appointment of service providers by MCST councils.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ms Joan Pereira noted that there have been instances where council members would bulldoze certain decisions through meetings for their own benefit, while Mr Gan Thiam Poh commented that all council members should be asked to disclose their interests.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing emphasised the need for checks and balances to ensure that service providers are appointed on their own merits, rather than by affiliation to any council member.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are all important points about good governance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under sections 60 and 61, all council members are expected to act honestly and exercise reasonable diligence in the discharge of their duties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The council member must also recuse himself from the discussion and voting on the matter, if pecuniary interest is involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MCSTs can also ensure that their contractual agreements with service providers contain expected levels of performance and/or service quality to facilitate greater transparency and tighter financial governance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MCSTs can also implement internal controls and procedures when selecting and appointing service providers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This could include requiring a minimum number of quotes to be solicited as part of the procurement procedure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To guide MCSTs, BCA's strata management guides, which I mentioned earlier, will highlight such good practices for reference.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan suggested that we consider the need for MAs to comply with some basic service standards, staff qualifications and audits of procurement processes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Service standards can be subjective and they also tend to vary according to the needs and preferences of different MCSTs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, our sense is that it is better for MCSTs to specify their expected service standards in their contractual agreements with the MAs instead.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we recognise the importance of having competent MAs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I mentioned earlier, we are working with industry associations to implement a voluntary accreditation system with the aim of improving the level of competency and professionalism of MAs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The BCA Academy also offers courses covering the strata management framework and the relevant rules and regulations, and we encourage MAs to make use of these training opportunities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah suggested that there should be an option for MCSTs to appoint MAs for shorter terms, shorter than three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Act allows MAs to be appointed for terms of up to three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, MCSTs already have the option of varying the term of appointment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of course, both parties would have to agree to the terms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In any case, the MA's performance must be reviewed at every AGM.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked how the Commissioner assesses proposed maintenance charge rates to ensure that they are justifiable, considering that the facilities have yet to be built.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Developers will need to take into account the costs for essential services like cleaning, security, utilities, insurances and maintenance of lifts and other common property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They should project these costs in relation to the development size, amenities provided, and the construction timeframe to factor in possible inflation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Developers can tap on their past experience in building and managing other properties to come up with reasonable estimates.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Commissioner may also require developers to submit additional information to justify the proposal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested that developers should be required to transfer at least three to six months' worth of maintenance funds to the MCSTs, while Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Louis Ng also asked related questions of what happens when the approved maintenance charges are subsequently found to be excessive or insufficient for the development, as the case may be.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The funds to be transferred are the balance of the maintenance charges which the developer has collected from SPs after handing over the keys to the units.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The handover period from the developer to the MCST is typically about a year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, accumulating a balance of three to six months will be quite a challenge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, it would run right smack into the concerns raised by Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Louis Ng, that there will be questions as to why after collecting fees meant to service a year's maintenance costs, you can have a three- to six-month balance to hand over.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Louis Ng's queries, the Commissioner actually approves the maximum rate of the maintenance charge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I shared earlier that this approved rate will be reflected in the prescribed Option to Purchase, as well as the Sale and Purchase Agreement forms.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This arrangement is the most flexible in meeting the needs of both developers and SPs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If the rates are found to be too high, developers have the option of revising the rate downwards without the need for the Commissioner's approval.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, the developer will need to obtain the consent of all purchasers and seek the Commissioner's approval again on the revised rate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To assess the validity of the developer's proposed revision, the Commissioner can ask for supporting documents like revised quotations from service providers and proof of purchasers' consent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: After the MCSTs are formed, of course, SPs can review and revise the maintenance charges at any general meeting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also spoke about the amendment to make maintenance charges known upfront to purchasers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She suggested taking the amendment a step further by making known the maintenance charge rates for the first three years as well as the estimated time and expenses involved for the first replacements of lifts, pumps and water tanks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The maximum rate proposed by developers would already reflect what SPs need to pay on average for the initial years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It may not be easy for the developers to provide accurate estimates of what it might cost to replace major equipment as replacement schedule would depend on several factors, including usage, maintenance and alternatives.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But it is not that it cannot be done.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These kinds of capital expenses are financed by sinking fund contributions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, MCSTs should conduct annual budget reviews to ensure that their sinking funds are adequate for the expected replacements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Melvin Yong spoke about placing a cap on the utilisation of management funds, while Mr Dennis Tan spoke about the fact that the practice of setting aside a budget or the expenditure by MCs, out of maintenance funds for social, educational, sporting as well as legal matters, is already quite common, and he felt that it will be an encumbrance to require general meetings and EOGMs to set the caps on these budgets, and for the MCs to go back to the general meeting to get approval.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Maintenance charges, as the name goes, are intended for maintenance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are, of course, MCSTs that would use some of this funding from time to time to organise events like festivals and celebrations which bring all the SPs together for bonding.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But from time to time, we also hear cases where SPs complain why maintenance charges are being used for things other than maintenance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, this amendment takes a step forward in regularising and facilitating some of these activities that are already happening, and which help to foster within developments a sense of activity and for people to come together.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Having said that, it is a good first step to ensure that there is some safeguard on the use and the extent of use of these funds, and it is up to the MC, together with the general meeting and the caucus of the general meeting, to agree on how the budget will be set.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As an additional safeguard, MCSTs can also introduce caps on related expenditure to minimise overspending.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee suggested that the rental fees for the leasing of common property to commercial entities should be channelled into the MCST's management fund, by way of a special resolution.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are also existing provisions to seek approval from the general body prior to the renting out of common property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The specific level of approval needed depends on the duration of the lease.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, 90% resolution is required for the MCST to lease out common property for more than three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, there is no further need to authorise the MCST to do so by way of a special resolution.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan asked about the threshold for invoking the provisions to place an MCST under official management was derived.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked about the rationale for introducing new sections 126A and 126B, if motions can already be passed at general meetings to resolve disputes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, while the preference is for MCSTs to resolve their differences at general meetings, this is not always possible even if there is a quorum present.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, the new provisions empower the Commissioner to exercise the power to intervene, but only as a last resort.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, health concerns might result from the accumulation of refuse, if not cleared.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Safety concerns could also arise from disrepair to buildings when maintenance has not been done.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And now to address the concerns of both Mr Louis Ng and Mr Dennis Tan as to the way in which it was crafted, and the manner in which the Commissioner will exercise this power and when he will do so and invoke the power to introduce an OM.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is very important to bear in mind that, keeping with the self-regulating principle of BMSMA, we believe that the Commissioner should only intervene at the behest of SPs of the MCST and as the last resort.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Furthermore, there are costs to be borne by the MCST if an OM is appointed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Hence, the decision should remain in the hands of the SPs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we are mindful not to be drawn into disputes and to allow the Commissioner and OM to be used as tools to facilitate the resolutions of disputes between different factions of MCSTs or different factions of SPs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the Commissioner will exercise his power sparingly and look at each fact or each circumstance and determine whether the health and safety of the SPs of the estate are, indeed, threatened before they invoke this measure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about BCA's plans to address the issue of developments with insufficient members to form a functional MC.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We recognise that some councils face challenges in identifying enough SPs to serve.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That said, most MCSTs do not face this issue because SPs generally recognise that it is in their interests to be active in managing their estates' affairs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Alternatively, any SP can apply to STB for an order to appoint an MA to assist with the running of the estate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the MA will report to the general body or general meeting.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On a related note, Mr Melvin Yong asked if there was a need to specify the composition of the council.
